args.title: checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks; rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: After the deploy of checkout-api v2.3.1 to production (us-east, us-west, eu-west), the service failed health checks with an error rate of about 18%. The v2.3.1-rc build had also been unhealthy in staging. checkout-api was rolled back in all regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. After the rollback, the service is healthy in all regions with an error rate of about 0.2%. Follow-up: find the root cause of the v2.3.1 failure, and find out why it was promoted even though the RC was unhealthy in staging.

trace.final:
checkout-api is back on v2.3.0 in all regions and passing health checks. I also opened SEV2 incident INC-0001, which paged on-call.

- **What was wrong:** v2.3.1 was live in us-east, us-west and eu-west, failing health checks with an error rate of about 18%.
- **Rollback:** I rolled back to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. Since it had already been healthy in production, this didn't need change-manager approval. After the rollback the service is healthy in all regions, with an error rate of about 0.2%.
- **Incident:** INC-0001 describes the failure, the rollback and the result. It also lists follow-ups: find the root cause of the v2.3.1 failure, and find out why it went to production even though its release candidate (v2.3.1-rc) had already failed health checks in staging.

content.text: Most recent healthy production release is v2.3.0.
